newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed, market quiet.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Prices mixed, market quiet.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mixed on Wednesday amid lackluster activity in a shortened holiday week, dealers said.
Dealers cited bearish factors such as diminished flour mill run times, ample nearby supply and slack demand.
Also, competing feed ingredients like hominy, gluten feed and soyhulls were available and less expensive, one North Carolina dealer said.
One dealer said millfeed prices were expected to trend lower "until we see some stability in the grain markets and I'm not talking about a one-day correction."

"It's green pastures in Texas and Oklahoma and the same old dance," he said, referring to livestock feeding on pastures. "Maybe in a few weeks, we will be singing a different song but we are in trouble until then."

A Minneapolis broker said he believed that demand has slackened because of the favorable weather conditions for good pastures. "This is typical summer doldrums and it will continue for a while," he said.
Some millfeed offers remained unchanged to higher because of reduced production during this U.S. Independence Day holiday week. The holiday is Friday.
